topic: Distributed Rate Desync Collapses Edge Breakers
postText:
During morning outpatient registration spikes at the healthcare facilities where I engineer backend services, static gateway rate limits failed us.

Every API gateway instance hammered a central Redis cluster using sliding-window Lua scripts to enforce client request quotas. When network latency spiked by just 40ms under heavy I/O, gateway worker threads stalled waiting for counter sync. Thousands of clinical requests slipped past stale thresholds within that brief synchronization window.

The result? A downstream lab retrieval service was hit with a 4x traffic burst while already running hot. Its thread pool exhausted in seconds. Client timeouts skyrocketed, flipping the edge circuit breaker to fully OPEN. One over-quota surge knocked out lab query endpoints across all hospital units.

We eliminated the remote bottleneck through three architectural shifts:

1. Token Leases over Atomic Counters: Gateways fetch token batches locally every second. When network sync drops, nodes enforce hard fallback limits locally without blocking.
2. Concurrency-Based Shedding (Vegas / Little's Law): Replaced static request-per-second ceilings with dynamic inflight concurrency tracking. If upstream latency climbs, the gateway throttles incoming requests before downstreams degrade.
3. Segmented Circuit Breaking: Isolated circuit states by route priority and client tenant so bulk reporting jobs cannot trip critical triage pathways.
